name: Hardware Verified
description: Arcade games on the MisterZine release tracker whose core was built and checked against the real board or its schematics: an owned or borrowed PCB, the author's own PAL/PROM dumps, the original schematics, logic analyzer or scope captures, or a published write-up of how the logic was derived from the board. Verified means built and checked against the real hardware, not that every behavior was tested. Positive only: a game without an entry means nothing. Entries are curated by hand from the core author's own public words, and each lists the links it rests on.
license: MiSTerZine Catalogue Licence (the CC BY 4.0 terms plus a source-neutrality condition), https://misterzine.fyi/releases/LICENSE.txt. Credit "MisterZine by Matija Erceg" and, where practical, link to https://misterzine.fyi.

fields.k: the release tracker's row key: the k field of releases/data.json and the #k deep link (https://misterzine.fyi/releases/#k)
fields.title: the game's title on the tracker when the entry was made (informational; titles can change, the key does not)
fields.rbfs: the shipped core file name(s) without the date stamp and .rbf extension (data.json core)
fields.setnames: the MAME set name(s) of the row (data.json sn)
fields.granted: the day the entry was added, YYYY-MM-DD
fields.reason: what the evidence shows, in plain words
fields.links: the evidence: the core author's own public pages

badges.title: Michael Jackson's Moonwalker
badges.reason: Built with a real Sega Moonwalker board on loan to the JT team. The System 18 schematics in the core's repository were reverse engineered during that hardware study, and the sync captures and screenshots used for comparison are published in its doc folder.

badges.title: Kicker
badges.reason: The JT team extracted full schematics from a Kicker board donated by Brian Schinzel. They also burnt test EPROMs to probe the custom chips, and reported what they found to the MAME team.

badges.title: Karate Champ: Player Vs Player
badges.reason: Built from the published schematics and an original two-player board donated by DJ Hardrich. The README says that hardware reference covers this two-player version, while the single-player Karate Champ was derived from MAME, so only this version carries the seal.

badges.title: Exed Exes
badges.reason: No schematics were available, so Jotego extracted them from an original Exed Exes board and built the core from them rather than from emulators. The extracted schematics are published with the core.

badges.title: The FairyLand Story
badges.reason: Based on schematics the JT team drew from an original FairyLand Story arcade board, which a fan sent them. The README notes the board turned out to be full of surprises.

badges.title: Vigilante
badges.reason: The JT team analysed an original Vigilante board together with the official schematics. The video timing was measured on the board and checked against the schematics.

badges.title: Rastan
badges.reason: The JT team analysed an original Rastan Saga board together with the official schematics.

badges.title: Ikari III - The Rescue
badges.reason: Verified against an Ikari III board donated to the project and against the Ikari III (A7007) schematics. Timing measurements were also taken from P.O.W. and Street Smart boards.

badges.title: P-47: The Freedom Fighter
badges.reason: Verified against an authentic P-47: The Freedom Fighter board bought by atrac17 for the project. The README also publishes the board's video timings, measured with a logic analyzer.

badges.title: Vimana
badges.reason: Built from the OutZone (TP-018) schematics and verified against two loaned Vimana (TP-019) boards.

badges.title: Terra Force
badges.reason: Verified against an authentic Nichibutsu Terra Force board and a bootleg board.

badges.title: The Next Space
badges.reason: Verified against an authentic The Next Space (A8004-1) board bought by atrac17.

badges.title: Nemesis
badges.reason: Based on Konami's Nemesis schematics and verified against several real boards: a Bubble System, a Salamander and a Salamander bootleg. The authors drew full schematics of the graphics board, modelled its chips from waveform captures of the originals, and wrote their own test program to measure sprites on a real board.

badges.title: ASO - Armored Scrum Object
badges.reason: The author captured the PAL chips of his own working Alpha Mission (ASO) board with a logic analyzer while building this core, and corrected their equations. The fixed equations were burnt to GAL chips and tested in the original board.

badges.title: TwinBee (Bubble System)
badges.reason: Built with a real Konami Bubble System board at hand, which the source code cites when explaining its bubble memory timing. The bubble memory controller chip is rebuilt cell by cell from a photo of its die.

badges.title: Jackal
badges.reason: A bootleg Jackal board was sourced for reverse engineering, and the logic is modelled to match the original board design as closely as possible. The audio filters are tuned to match both bootleg and original boards.

badges.title: Computer Space
badges.reason: The original schematics were copied wire by wire and gate by gate, so the core is a circuit-level copy of the machine. Timer values, the star field and the video sync were checked against measurements taken from real Computer Space boards.

badges.title: Klax
badges.reason: Built from the Klax board schematics and the dumped on-board PALs, with MAME only as a cross-reference. Where the two disagree the core follows the hardware, and each difference is documented.

badges.title: Star Wars
badges.reason: The vector generator is rebuilt cycle-exact from the original Atari schematics. The author published his hand-verified transcription of that logic, the blueprint the core was built from.

badges.title: Pong
badges.reason: A Verilog implementation based on the original Atari schematics. Pong's analog circuits are simulated in digital logic, and the author says every signal should be accurate to the edges of the system clock.

badges.title: Bomber Man
badges.reason: Built with a real Irem M90 board on loan, which the author used for all of the core's timing measurements and to analyse its GA25 graphics chip.

badges.title: R-Type Leo
badges.reason: The author thanks Mark for his R-Type Leo board, and the core's repository holds chip-by-chip notes on the board and KiCad schematics of the Irem M92 board set.

badges.title: Iron Horse
badges.reason: A bootleg Iron Horse board was sourced for reverse engineering, and the logic is modelled to match the original as closely as possible, down to the board's switchable audio filters.

badges.title: Escape from the Planet of the Robot Monsters
badges.reason: Refined through testing and benchmarking against an original dedicated cabinet and board, with clocks, raster, memory map and the sprite line buffer verified against Atari's schematics. The README separates what is schematic-verified, what is approximate and what was measured against real-cabinet captures.

badges.title: The Empire Strikes Back
badges.reason: The Empire Strikes Back runs on the Star Wars hardware as a conversion kit, and the core's vector generator is rebuilt cycle-exact from the original Atari schematics. The author published his hand-verified transcription of that logic, the blueprint the core was built from.

badges.title: Major Havoc
badges.reason: Reconstructs Major Havoc's dual-processor hardware from Atari's schematics. The cabinet audio defaults to gains and a filter measured from original cabinet recordings.
